sources.title: Johanna Regev and colleagues, Radiocarbon chronology of Iron Age Jerusalem (PNAS, 2024)
sources.note: Direct PMC challenged; full original indexed article read with exact-title query plus undetermined. Abstract and section The12th to10th centuries BC:103dates/fiveareas and18early samples, mostly building-material inclusions. Occupation character explicitly undetermined; not proof of a palace or empire.

sources.title: Yosef Garfinkel and colleagues, Second radiocarbon dating project at Khirbet Qeiyafa (Radiocarbon, 2015)
sources.note: Publisher abstract directly read:17burnt olive pits in destruction-layer jar,4split between two laboratories, approximately1000BCE result. Title has a stronger political identification than the data alone can establish.

sources.title: Alexander Fantalkin and Israel Finkelstein, Date and territorial affiliation of Khirbet Qeiyafa (Tel Aviv, 2017)
sources.note: Publisher direct fetch failed. Authors’ primary abstract read as reproduced in EBSCOhost https://openurl.ebsco.com/fulltext/gcd%3A123149866 via exact title query: date/territorial affiliation disputed; material features have northern associations. No inaccessible detailed argument quoted.

sources.title: Yossi Garfinkel and Saar Ganor, Khirbat Qeiyafa: 2013, Israel Antiquities Authority
sources.note: Direct excavation report read, AreaA/F and numbered conclusions3-4. Observed large structure, thicker walls, storehouse, fingerprint jar handles. Political assignment and palace function remain excavators’ interpretations. Byzantine winepress and seventh-century agricultural tower not assigned to tenth century.

sources.title: Yosef Garfinkel, The Iron Age City of Khirbet Qeiyafa (2017), author-uploaded chapter
sources.note: Direct author-uploaded primary chapter text read. Printed pp.121-122: courtyards, tabun ovens, adjoining rooms; pp.124-125: coastal grinding stones, basalt tools and imports; Excavator’s historical identification explicitly qualified elsewhere.

sources.title: Yosef Garfinkel and Madeleine Mumcuoglu, Triglyphs and Recessed Doorframes (IEJ, 2013)
sources.note: Author-uploaded primary article directly read, abstract and Building C10 context, pp.135-163. Stone building model, recessed doorway and roof triglyphs. Temple comparison presented as scholarly comparison, not identification of an excavated Jerusalem temple.

sources.title: Guy Bloch and colleagues, Industrial apiculture in the Jordan valley (PNAS, 2010)
sources.note: Original paper abstract directly read via PubMed. TelRehov10th-early9thcentury clay hives and workers/drones/larvae/pupae; morphology matches Anatolian bees, authors retain ancient distribution change OR import alternatives. Comparative regional evidence, no royal ownership assertion.

sources.title: The Jewish Museum, Tel Dan Stele exhibition text
sources.note: Direct one-page museum PDF read. Ninth-century Aramaic House of David, fragments1993/1994, dynastic evidence later than David. Museum narrative’s stronger united-monarchy statements are not adopted as independent proof.

sources.title: Ashmolean Museum, Focus on Judaism: royal jar handles and Hannah seal
sources.note: Direct PDF text read: page2 item3 gives c700BCE Jerusalem jar handles and exact l-m-l-k / belonging to the king; page1 item2 gives750-700BCE Lachish seal / belonging to Hannah. Screenshot service cache missed. Latin transcription only, no invented ancient glyph facsimile. Broader speculative economic assertions omitted.

sources.title: Piers D. Mitchell and colleagues, Giardia and dysentery in Iron Age Jerusalem (Parasitology, 2023)
sources.note: Original research abstract read directly:2latrines,7th and7th-early6thcenturies, Giardia antigens both positive in3repeatedtests. Figures identify stone seats. Comparative laterJudah health evidence, not tenth-century David/Solomon. No universal prevalence asserted.

sources.title: Ira Spar, Cyrus and the Judean Diaspora, Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.note: Direct full museum essay read, Israelite and Archaeological Evidence sections. Northern state conquest by721, Jerusalem586, later cuneiform business archives and diaspora continuity. Used for later centuries; opening unqualified David state narrative, simplistic Cyrus Cylinder inference and obsolete archive publication status not adopted.
